title: Not my cup of tea
body:
I really wanted this to be my long-term laptop because it looks great on paper: OLED display, premium design, haptic touchpad, Windows Hello, and a modern “AI PC” platform. The screen is legitimately beautiful, and the touchpad is one of the best I’ve used on any Windows laptop.

But the more I use it, the more I feel like I might return it mainly because the daily experience isn’t matching the premium price.

The biggest dealbreaker for me is the typing experience. The keyboard feels overly clicky/clacky and doesn’t have the satisfying, solid feel I expect from a “premium” machine. Obviously that's just preference, and it sounds minor until you’re using it for school/work but over time it becomes irritating and has annoyed others in meetings. I type a lot, and I need a keyboard that feels smooth, stable, and quiet enough to enjoy using. This one doesn’t. It feels more hollow than expected and just not enjoyable long term.

The second major issue is battery life. I’m not seeing “all-day battery” behavior at all, even with normal usage. Watching YouTube, browsing, or doing basic productivity tasks drains it faster than it should, and that defeats the whole purpose of this class of laptop. It’s the kind of battery drain where you start thinking: If it’s like this now, what will it look like in 6–12 months? At times it feels like I’m losing battery almost fast enough that I’m always checking the percentage instead of just using the device.

And lastly, the 2-in-1 design hasn’t been as practical as I thought. It’s constantly shifting modes if you adjust the hinge too far back, and that gets old quickly especially when using it casually on the couch or in bed.

It has some amazing strengths (especially the screen and touchpad), but if the typing and battery experience aren’t there, it’s hard to justify keeping it. At this point I’m leaning toward returning it unless something changes dramatically after more updates and optimization.

title: Best Windows laptop I’ve ever owned
body:
I’ve owned laptops since 1987 (the first had just two floppy drives), and this HP Omnibook Ultra Flip is the best Windows laptop I’ve ever used.

In fact, it’s a close second to my M4 Macbook Air, which is a zephyr among laptops and sets a pretty high bar to surpass. The Omnibook Ultra is just slightly wider than the Macbook Air, the same depth and only a little thicker when closed. And it is only 2 ounces heavier. On the other hand, the Ultra 9 288v processor is about 20% slower than the M4, according to some reviews, and it is also a less energy efficient chip, so battery life is not as good as the Macbook Air. 

Nonetheless, I really like the Omnibook Ultra. It’s a light and very capable laptop, and with 32 GB memory and 2 TB storage, it pretty much eliminates those common limitations. But the best feature is its 3K OLED display. It is truly gorgeous. Colors pop and details are sharp and crisp. A small disadvantage is its speakers are primarily on the bottom of the case, so it can sound muffled when on your lap. That is less noticeable on a desk.

Last but not least, it has both facial recognition and a very good fingerprint reader, so Windows Hello rarely insists that I enter my pin, unlike the Lenovo Yoga Slim 9i (a very similar laptop) which does not do facial recognition and had a rarely successful fingerprint reader, so Windows Hello was very annoying on it. 

If you can find the Omnibook Ultra on sale (Best Buy recently had it $600 off list price), it can be a bargain, but even at full list price, it’s a great laptop.

title: Omni Book Ultra  14" Ultra 9 Intel-chip
body:
12-8 2025 I have had this OmniBook Ultra-9 for about 60 days now. 
 I switched  from another brand that had 3 features I liked, I'll comment below.   This Ultra has all the specifications I was interested in and the Ultra 9 Intel chip is great. The pricing was great... and,  with the  Best-Buy membership guaranteed a warranty.  The battery is working well and  overall the performance for what I need is fine, no issues.

1. The Laptop "outer covering" seems like an aluminum - its sort of cold to touch, especially if on the road.  The other brand had a hard -rubberized outer-shell, I really liked it and if anything would show show scuffs and not damaged.
2. This "Synoptic touch pad" on this HP seem larger than it needs to be. In my opinion it could easily be 1.25 inches smaller in width.  It gets in my way when resting my hands on the laptop when typing. Smaller have made this awesome!  Is this size really necessary on a 14" Laptop? 
3. I wish it had an extra port or two more than what it came with.  I know that would have affected the price and not likely the size.  I knew when I purchased it what it had,  so I am not surprised. It's just a comment.    I bought a small docking unit for the other connections just in case...

Overall being 14" inches its great, I didn't need a larger bulkier laptop,  when traveling.  The Ultra9 Intel-chip is good,  the screen pixels are great,  matched with 32  ram... 

3 things I wish were different, are NOT deal breakers!
 Overall happy with the purchase,  thanks to BestBuy!

body: I recently purchased an open-box HP Omnibook Ultra Flip laptop, and I am impressed with its condition. There are no scratches or dents on the laptop, and it looks almost brand new. The performance is smooth, and the display is crisp and clear. The flip feature works perfectly, making it easy to switch between laptop and tablet modes. Overall, it’s a great deal for the price, and I’m happy with my purchase.

title: Very God!!
body: Very god!!It's very good, it's light, it has good resolution, it's fast, it has a good screen size, I'm simply delighted with it.

title: Great build with stunning display
body: So far its fast and the display is beautiful.  I will give a 6 month update on this piece of machine. This is a beast 32g ultra. Built quality is top tier.

title: Small and Powerful
body: Yes. I am impressed. I originally purchased the 16g/1tb Intel Core Ultra 7 and soon realized I was in desperate need of more space because I like running a kazillion things apps at the same time. This model is enough space and then some. This laptop is ultra portable. I purchased the HP Active Rechargeable Tilt Pen MPP 2 to use with. I love being able to flip it around and watch movies in the "tent" position. This thing is fast and the battery life is amazing. For the price it should  have at least come with the pen. I am happy with this 2 in 1.

title: Don't recommend
body: Computer freezes, need to turn on and off the bluetooth daily because devices won't connect, especially when coming off of sleep.

title: Bad start. GREAT finish.
body: After 4 hours on the phone trying to purchase a laptop, I had to give up, we just were not able to make it work. I decided I really did want that laptop. I ended up having to go to a store in person to get this order to go through, but the staff there was phenominal! It only took 8 minutes to explain the problem to them and check out. My computer came next day. Setup was easy and this laptop has more capabilities than my previous 4 year old desktop had. I haven't needed any help, but I am sure if I do, they are only a phone call away. So it didn't start out so well, but the staff at the store were stars. I am one happy customer!

title: Very good option to consider
body:
I came from a 6 years old Yoga 9I. In my case I noted pretty well the improvement on performance. Lovely screen with lovely colors and definition.

The chip is the best one you can have from intel Lunar Lake series.

The DEL button is exactly next ot it of the power button, for make doesn't make sense at all... something to consider.

The batterry is very good, around 12 hours.

It works pretty well on really hard and heavy excel files, at least 8-10 open Chormes tabs, outlook with lots and lots of Gb and emails into it, some youtube ambient music and some Teams conferences, all of them at same time, same day.... probably those 32Gb of RAM helps a lot

title: Great Laptop
body: Great laptop all around. Lightweight, premium build, look, and feel. Super responsive and fast for all kinds of tasks. It even handles light gaming pretty well to very well.

title: A Powerful laptop, slick and perfect for travel
body:
This laptop is exactly what I needed. I frequently run multiple applications at once, and the 32GB of memory makes a significant difference compared to my previous 16GB laptop. It’s sleek and features three USB-C ports. Initially, I was concerned this might be an issue, but I’ve been able to connect everything via Bluetooth, so I rarely need the ports—aside from charging other devices.

The 3K OLED screen is absolutely stunning and something I didn’t realize I needed. The vibrant colors and deep contrast make a noticeable difference, and it's incredibly easy on my eyes, especially during long work sessions.

The laptop is impressively lightweight, with a battery life of about four hours, and the compact charger is convenient for travel. It runs completely silently; unlike my previous laptops, where I could always hear the fan at some point, this one remains quiet even when multiple programs are running in the background.

I also purchased a Bamboo pen, which pairs seamlessly with the laptop. The only downside is that it was at the top of my budget, but overall, it has been well worth the investment.

title: Fast
body: Fast computer and lightweight. Display looks great.

title: Get this
body: This computer works great for me. Seems like the best processor in the game and so worth the price especially when it goes on sale. Aesthetics are nice and really light and durable. Took it on a 5 day work trip and worked great. I typically use 3 screens but was able to just use this laptop on the road and had no issues whatsoever

title: Love it
body: I like that this is compact. Easy to carry. It's more than what I need  for daily browsing.

title: What a piece of CRAP
body: Sure everything's all nice and pretty and polished for HP, however you only received one USBC port. That leaves you running peripherals on Bluetooth. No matter how many times you go into the Bluetooth settings advanced properties anything you cannot set your mouse to wake the PC with the mouse. Completely grayed out. My hands are rather large, so that means I'm consistently hitting the trackpad. Disable the trackpad, and expected my mouse to work, which is a Microsoft mouse, and wake up the device. Can't walk away for 5 minutes without having to touch the screen, turn my Bluetooth off, then turn my Bluetooth back on, and hope to God that it reconnects the Bluetooth mouse. If all else fails, I get to restart the computer remove the device and then added as a new device. I will be taking this piece of sh!+ back immediately!
